edits.old: Atlas Resource Policies add organization-wide configuration guardrails to RBAC; project exceptions allow narrower application. Cluster tier caps are a documented cost-control use. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-18)
edits.new: Atlas Resource Policies are organization-wide controls that let Organization Owners constrain the cluster configuration options available to developers. They are allow-by-default and apply on top of what a user's Atlas role allows. Specific projects can be excluded, so exceptions are possible. A documented policy type enforces minimum and maximum cluster tiers and auto-scaling sizes. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/atlas-resource-policies.md

evidence.quote: Atlas Resource Policies are controls that enable [`Organization Owners`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/reference/user-roles.md#mongodb-authrole-Organization-Owner) to constrain the specific configuration options available to developers when they create or configure Atlas clusters.
By default, Atlas Resource Policies are organization-wide. These policies automatically enforce standards across all projects and clusters within the organization.

You can exclude specific projects from an Atlas Resource Policy. This functionality allows most projects to inherit consistent organization-wide standards while enabling exceptions for cases with unique requirements.

Atlas Resource Policies are allow-by-default. If no Atlas Resource Policies exist, users can perform all actions on Atlas clusters that their [Atlas user role](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/reference/user-roles.md#std-label-user-roles) allows.

this policy prevents users from provisioning, updating, or [auto-scaling](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/cluster-autoscaling.md#std-label-cluster-autoscaling) clusters to a tier above or below a specified threshold.

A financial services organization might combine disk size limits, topology requirements, and shard count minimums with additional controls like cluster tier restrictions to create a comprehensive governance framework.
